points.reason: The clocked process exposes rs1_i through res_o and can overwrite or withhold it by selecting zero according to condition and valid_cmd.
The condition wire controls whether res_o receives rs1_i or zero, so tampering can alter or block the result, but the wire does not itself expose the result data.
The command decode gates the result assignment, allowing an attacker to reject a valid result or force the zero path, but it does not carry the result word.
The comparison wire derives the zero predicate from rs2_i, and changing that predicate changes whether the result path passes rs1_i or writes zero.
The condition carries the comparison predicate into the result decision, so its value can be inferred from the selected result and can alter or block that result.
The result process exposes the operand's zero or nonzero effect through res_o and can select zero instead of the intended rs1-derived result.
The condition wire is the internal selection decision, and its value can be inferred from res_o or changed to select or suppress the rs1_i result.
The rs2_zero predicate feeds the selection decision, so it can influence the selected result and its value can be inferred from that result.
The result process exposes the decision through the choice of rs1_i versus zero and permits the decision path to alter or block the returned result.
The command decode directly determines valid_o, so changing it can falsely validate an unsupported operation or reject a supported one.
The same validity decode gates the conditional result process, so an invalid or suppressed decode can prevent the operation's result from being used.
